content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

message.content:
Below are three ways you can create a Compute Engine instance that has an **RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Why you might choose it |
|--------|-----------------|--------------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Quick, scriptable, works from any shell |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/instances` | Useful if you’re building a custom integration |
| **Python client** | `google.cloud.compute_v1.InstancesClient()` | Great for Python‑centric automation |

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="n1-standard-8" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="100GB" \
  --boot-disk-type="pd-ssd" \
  --boot-disk-device-name="$INSTANCE_NAME" \
  --maintenance-policy="TERMINATE" \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=./startup.sh \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --guest-accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" \
  --no-boot-disk-auto-delete \
  --no-shielded-secure-boot \
  --no-shielded-vtpm \
  --no-shielded-integrity-monitoring
```

> **Notes**
> * `--machine-type="n1-standard-8"` gives you 8 vCPUs and 30 GB RAM – enough for most workloads that need an RTX A6000.
> * `--accelerator` and `--guest-accelerator` are required to attach the GPU.
> * `--metadata-from-file startup-script=./startup.sh` lets you run a script on first boot (e.g., install NVIDIA drivers).  
>   Example `startup.sh`:

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# Install NVIDIA driver
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
```

---

## 2. REST API (curl)

```bash
# Variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth print-access-token)

# JSON payload
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_JSON <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# POST request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_JSON"
```

> **Tip** – If you’re using a service account key file, you can obtain an access token with:
> ```bash
> ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth activate-service-account --key-file=path/to/key.json && gcloud auth print-access-token)
> ```

---

## 3. Python Client Library

```python
from google.cloud import compute_v1
from google.oauth2 import service_account

# Credentials
creds = service_account.Credentials.from_service_account_file(
    "path/to/key.json",
    scopes=["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"],
)

# Client
client = compute_v1.InstancesClient(credentials=creds)

# Instance details
project = "my-gcp-project"
zone = "us-central1-a"
instance_name = "rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# Build the instance
instance = compute_v1.Instance()
instance.name = instance_name
instance.machine_type = f"zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8"

# Disk
disk = compute_v1.AttachedDisk()
disk.boot = True
disk.auto_delete = True
disk.initialize_params = compute_v1.AttachedDiskInitializeParams()
disk.initialize_params.source_image = "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts"
disk.initialize_params.disk_size_gb = 100
disk.initialize_params.disk_type = f"projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
instance.disks = [disk]

# Network
nic = compute_v1.NetworkInterface()
nic.network = "global/networks/default"
nic.access_configs = [compute_v1.AccessConfig(name="External NAT", type_="ONE_TO_ONE_NAT")]
instance.network_interfaces = [nic]

# GPU
gpu = compute_v1.AcceleratorConfig()
gpu.accelerator_type = f"projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
gpu.accelerator_count = 1
instance.guest_accelerators = [gpu]

# Service account
sa = compute_v1.ServiceAccount()
sa.email = "default"
sa.scopes = ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
instance.service_accounts = [sa]

# Metadata (startup script)
meta_item = compute_v1.Metadata.Items()
meta_item.key = "startup-script"
meta_item.value = "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
instance.metadata = compute_v1.Metadata(items=[meta_item])

# Create the instance
operation = client.insert(project=project, zone=zone, instance_resource=instance)

# Wait for completion
print(f"Creating instance {instance_name}…")
operation.result()  # blocks until the operation completes
print("Instance created.")
```

> **Prerequisites**
> * Install the library: `pip install google-cloud-compute`
> * Enable the Compute Engine API in your project.

---

## Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | **Project & Zone** – set correctly |
| ✅ | **Machine type** – at least `n1-standard-8` |
| ✅ | **GPU** – `nvidia-tesla-a6000` |
| ✅ | **Boot disk** – Ubuntu 20.04 LTS (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | **Startup script** – installs NVIDIA driver |
| ✅ | **Service account** – has `cloud-platform` scope |
| ✅ | **Billing enabled** – GPU instances require billing |

---

### Common Pitfalls

| Problem | Fix |
|---------|-----|
| “GPU type not available in this zone” | Use a zone that supports RTX A6000 (e.g., `us-central1-a`, `europe-west4-a`). |
| “Insufficient quota” | Request a GPU quota increase in the GCP console. |
| “Driver not installed” | Verify the startup script runs; check serial port logs (`gcloud compute instances get-serial-port-output`). |

---

### Next Steps

1. **Create the instance** using one of the methods above.
2. **Verify GPU visibility** once the instance is running:

   ```bash
   gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" --command "nvidia-smi"
   ```

3. **Install any additional software** you need (CUDA, cuDNN, etc.) on the instance.
